questions.question: In TCP/IP, which component is responsible for ordering packets and reassembling them at the destination?
questions.explanation: TCP breaks messages into packets, guarantees delivery and reassembles them in order; IP handles addressing.

questions.question: In the context of e-commerce websites, cookies are:

options.A: Advertisements that open underneath the current page
options.B: Text files stored in the browser about the user's interaction with a website
options.C: Small programs that encrypt card numbers during checkout
options.D: Server logs that record only payment failures

questions.explanation: Cookies are text files stored in a browser that relate to a user's interaction with a website.

questions.concept: Memory allocation time of linked list vs array
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares memory allocation in arrays and linked lists?

options.A: Array memory is allocated at compile time; linked list memory at run time
options.B: Array memory is allocated at run time; linked list memory at compile time
options.C: Both allocate memory only at run time
options.D: Both allocate memory only at compile time

questions.explanation: Arrays have static memory allocated at compile time, while linked lists are dynamic, allocating memory at run time so they can grow and shrink.

questions.concept: goto is the jump statement transferring control
questions.question: Which C++ statement, also known as a jump statement, transfers control to another (labelled) part of the program?
questions.explanation: goto transfers control to a labelled statement elsewhere in the program. continue only skips the current iteration and switch selects among cases.

questions.question: In which year did IBM introduce the first personal computer for home users?
questions.explanation: IBM introduced the first PC for home users in 1981. Apple's Macintosh came in 1984 and the Intel 4004 microprocessor in 1971.

questions.concept: Two-way infinite tape TM as a listed variation
questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a variation of the Turing machine?
questions.explanation: Listed variations are multiple track, two-way infinite tape, multi-tape, multi-tape multi-head and multi-dimensional tape TMs.

questions.question: Which open-source framework stores and processes large amounts of data across a network of computers and is a key technology for big data analytics in the cloud?
questions.explanation: Hadoop is the open-source framework for distributed storage and processing of big data. Pandas is a Python analysis library and VMware is a virtualization/private cloud vendor.

questions.question: Which operating system is a typical example of a Command Line (Character User) Interface?
questions.explanation: In a CLI the user types keyboard commands; MS-DOS is the standard example, while Windows is the GUI example.

questions.concept: readline() returns empty string at EOF
questions.question: What does readline() return once the end of the file has been reached?
questions.explanation: readline() returns an empty string at EOF, which is why a loop such as while str: stops reading.

questions.question: Which testing type is also called database testing, in which the GUI is not involved?
questions.explanation: Back-end testing is database testing and does not involve the GUI; interface testing is GUI testing.

questions.concept: Sum of LBA and Moore machine tuple counts
questions.question: If you add the number of tuples in the formal definition of a Linear Bounded Automaton to the number of tuples in a Moore machine, what total do you get?
questions.explanation: An LBA is an 8-tuple and a Moore machine is a 6-tuple, so 8 + 6 = 14.

questions.question: Which statement about IoT input components is FALSE?

options.A: A photoresistor light sensor is an analog sensor
options.B: A microphone is a digital sensor
options.C: A keyboard is a digital sensor
options.D: A push button is a digital sensor

questions.explanation: A microphone produces a continuously varying signal and is not a digital sensor. A photoresistor is analog, while push buttons and keyboards are digital.

questions.question: Host-to-host delivery and node-to-node delivery are the responsibilities of which layers, respectively?

options.A: Transport layer and Data Link layer
options.C: Data Link layer and Transport layer
options.D: Network layer and Data Link layer

questions.explanation: Host-to-host (end-to-end, process-to-process) is Transport; node-to-node is Data Link.

questions.concept: Final step of a project is its outcome
questions.question: Among the steps for solving a project (identification, defining a plan, fixing time frame and processing, guidance and monitoring, outcome), which step comes last?
questions.explanation: The project steps end with the outcome of the project, after guidance and monitoring.

questions.question: Uppercase 'A' is 65 in ASCII and each lowercase letter is 32 more than its uppercase form. What is the 7-bit binary ASCII code of lowercase 'c'?

questions.concept: Round robin average waiting time with quantum 4
questions.question: Processes P1, P2 and P3 arrive at time 0 in that order with CPU bursts of 24 ms, 3 ms and 3 ms. Using Round Robin with a time quantum of 4 ms, what is the average waiting time?
questions.explanation: Timeline: P1 0-4, P2 4-7, P3 7-10, P1 10-30. Waiting times are P1 = 6, P2 = 4, P3 = 7, giving 17 / 3 = about 5.67 ms.

questions.question: Linear search is also known as:
questions.explanation: Linear search compares elements one by one, so it is also called sequential search or serial search.

questions.concept: List and string cannot be concatenated
questions.question:
What happens when the following code runs?
lst = [1, 2]
print(lst + '3')
questions.explanation: The + operator joins a list only with another list. A list cannot be concatenated with a string, so TypeError is raised.

questions.question: Which malware is created mainly to generate revenue for its developer by displaying advertisements?
questions.explanation: Adware is malware created to generate revenue by displaying advertisements; it is usually annoying and may show unsafe links.

questions.question: Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), regarded as one of the early forms of e-commerce, was developed in which decade?
questions.explanation: EDI was developed in the 1960s, well before web-based online shopping, which is why it is called an early form of e-commerce.

questions.question: Full-duplex communication may be implemented using:

options.A: Two physically separate simplex lines or a single shared channel
options.D: Only a single simplex line that switches direction

questions.explanation: Full duplex may use two separate simplex lines or one shared channel whose capacity is split between both directions.

questions.concept: Complete clause order of SQL query
questions.question: Which sequence shows the correct order of clauses in an SQL query?

options.A: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
options.B: SELECT, WHERE, FROM, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, HAVING
options.C: SELECT, FROM, GROUP BY, WHERE, HAVING, ORDER BY
options.D: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, HAVING, GROUP BY, ORDER BY

questions.explanation: The order is SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY; HAVING follows GROUP BY because it filters grouped aggregates.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recommended practice for combating malware?

options.A: Share login credentials only with close friends
options.B: Delay security patches to keep the system fast
options.C: Prefer pirated software from popular websites
options.D: Scan removable storage devices before using them

questions.explanation: Recommended practices include scanning removable devices, using legitimate software, applying security patches and never sharing passwords or login credentials.

questions.concept: Return value of main used by runtime library
questions.question: In C++, the value returned from main() is used by:
questions.explanation: main() is the starting point of execution, and its return value is passed back to and used by the runtime library.

questions.concept: Database following Codd's rules is a True RDBMS
questions.question: What is a database that follows all of Codd's 12 rules called?
questions.explanation: If a database follows Codd's 12 rules it is called a True RDBMS, ensuring consistency, accessibility and integrity.
